key_insight: A memory-augmented, symmetry-preserving graph neural network can learn reduced Lagrangian turbulent transport and recover key multi-particle statistics in homogeneous isotropic turbulence.
engineering_relevance: This offers a scalable data-driven surrogate for turbulent particle transport, useful for fast simulation and reduced-order modeling in multiphase flow and dispersion applications.
method: Mori--Zwanzig finite-memory expansion over present and delayed particle-neighborhood graphs
Equivariant message-passing GNN predicts acceleration while enforcing permutation, Galilean, rotational, and reflection symmetries
Autoregressive rollout used to test long-horizon dynamics and unseen observables
evidence_signal: Trained on direct numerical simulation data, the model reproduces intermittent acceleration tails, single-particle and pair dispersion, and four-particle tetrad geometry during evaluation.
watch_item: Performance depends on learned memory depth and high-quality DNS training data, so extrapolation to different turbulence regimes or particle types may require retraining.
paper_title: Learning turbulent transport via Mori--Zwanzig graph neural networks
